tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Harborview demo: rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (55 live words, zero room labels). Holabird proves the live-text lane works (92/109 named). v2 = productize the M3 tiles spike as opt-in 'read labels (AI)' + callout-vs-room noise filter.

prep.what: Add an opt-in AI label-reading mode via MiniMax tiles for firms where PDFTron outlines all text, plus a noise filter to strip callouts and stair arrows from room names.
prep.understand: The free live-text lane finds zero labels when PDFTron outlines text — it returns 55 morphological words but none are room names. The M3 tiles spike (`run_labels_m3tiles.py`) tiles the PDF into image chunks, sends each to MiniMax vision, and merges the read labels back onto room polygons. It runs ~4.3 min/sheet and costs money, so it must be an opt-in action gated by a metered-credits event (§7a). Holabird shows the noise problem: live-text finds 'UP' (stair), 'FEC', and multi-word general notes alongside real room names — the callout filter is the quality layer.
approach: Open `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` and understand the tiling parameters (tile size, overlap, MiniMax call, how label polygons are merged back to room polygons by centroid proximity).

Design the productization hook: a `§7a metered-credits event` in the service so AI label-reading is an explicit opt-in button — never fires automatically. Plan where MINIMAX_AI key lives on the VPS (`.env` + the existing secrets pattern).

Build the callout-vs-room filter as a small classifier: stair labels = short all-caps with cardinal direction ('UP', 'DN'); FEC/equipment = alphanumeric codes with dashes; general notes = contains punctuation or >3 words; real room names = 1–3 capitalized words. Apply post-MiniMax before persisting labels.
Wire the tiles lane into a new service route under the opt-in flag; the route should accept a `project_id` and return label results that the React review UI can apply in one click.
resources: `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` — the spike to productize
MiniMax vision API docs (model `abab6.5s-chat` or vision endpoint, tile image format)
`engine/labels.py` — current live-text lane to extend alongside the tiles lane
`service/routes.py` — find the §7a metered-credits event pattern to copy
VPS `.env` secrets pattern from `docs/README-SERVICE.md` for MINIMAX_AI key placement

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: `engine/assemblies.py` scaffolded (assemblies-lite). Full version = room classification → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries). The last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Complete the assemblies engine: map room classification → trade quantities (floor SF, wall paint SF, LF baseboard, door count) using wall height and CSI formulas, then emit them as rows in the export Excel.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` has a scaffold from assemblies-lite. A full assembly ties a room classification (e.g. 'bedroom', 'corridor', 'bathroom') to a list of assembly specs — each spec names a trade, a formula (floor_sf * 1.1 for flooring with 10% waste; perimeter * height for wall paint; perimeter for baseboard LF), and a CSI division. Wall height is not in the PDF; it comes from a project default or hard default (8 ft). The Excel lane (`build_sheet_takeoff`) currently emits raw area rows; assemblies adds a second derived layer.
approach: Read `engine/assemblies.py` to see the scaffold shape: what assembly spec dict it expects, what classification-to-assembly map is started (if any).

Define the assembly spec table as a Python dict: at minimum floor (area × 1.1 waste → flooring SF), wall_paint (perimeter × height → paint SF), ceiling_paint (area → paint SF), baseboard (perimeter → LF). Add CSI codes: 09 91 23 interior painting, 09 65 00 resilient flooring, 06 20 00 finish carpentry.
Implement `apply_assemblies(rooms, wall_height_ft, spec_table)` → list of assembly rows. Each row: room_id, trade, csi, formula_key, qty, unit.
Extend `build_sheet_takeoff` in `engine/excel.py` to call `apply_assemblies` and write assembly rows as a new 'Assemblies' tab or inline after the room SF block.
Write unit tests: feed a bedroom (area=150, perimeter=52, height=8) through the assembler — assert floor SF=165, wall paint SF=416, baseboard LF=52. Run `pytest` service suite (expect 19/19).

`engine/excel.py` + `build_sheet_takeoff` — where to wire the new assembly rows
CSI MasterFormat reference: Div 09 Finishes (09 91 23 interior painting, 09 65 00 resilient flooring), Div 06 (06 20 00 finish carpentry/baseboard)

tasks.title: Door recall round 2 + bi-fold / cased-opening recall
tasks.notes: Door recall is THE constraint blocking global SEAL_FT relax. Bi-fold detection shipped (scallop-ink). t15 (localseal guard) makes added chords safe. Target: chord coverage >0.6 (currently 0.00 on holabird/mitchell/washington/merrimack; 0.32 dental).

prep.what: Raise opening chord recall on the 4 firms with 0% chord coverage, pushing the localseal guard from a safety net into an accuracy gain.
prep.understand: t15 (localseal guard) proved that chord coverage is the bottleneck: 0.00 on 4 of 12 corpus sheets means the global `SEAL_FT` blanket cannot be retired. Bi-fold detection shipped via scallop-ink. Symbol-based detectors failed on furniture noise. 'Raster-gap detection' means scanning the wall-pixel raster for actual breaks — a pixel gap in the wall layer at a room boundary IS an opening, regardless of what symbol caused it. The localseal guard makes adding a bad chord safe (it self-reverts on merge), so the risk of false chords is now low.
approach: Run `docs/spike/w13_localseal_guard.py` on the corpus to get the current per-firm chord-coverage baseline. Inspect why holabird/mitchell/washington/merrimack get 0.00 — log what the detector finds vs what the GT rooms have.

Prototype a raster-gap detector in `engine/doors.py`: for each room boundary segment, scan the sealed-wall raster for horizontal/vertical runs of background pixels ≥ N px wide. Mask out regions with known furniture-noise signatures (blobs far from wall centerlines).
Test against the low-coverage sheets: target dental (0.32 → 0.6+) first, then one zero-coverage sheet. Verify gauntlet 81/81 stays clean with `--profile holabird` after changes.
Re-run `w13_localseal_guard.py`; if coverage crosses 0.6 on ≥2 new sheets, that's the signal to activate localseal there and queue the re-run of the full board.
resources: `docs/spike/w13_localseal_guard.py` — chord coverage benchmark to run first
`engine/doors.py` — current bi-fold + door detection code
`engine/sealfill.py` — `guard_relax`, localseal coverage guard logic
Gauntlet corpus: holabird, dental, brook_p4 PDFs + 81/81 baseline

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height. Add wall/ceiling height input (project default + per-room override). Wall paint SF/room = perimeter × height. The seeder currently drops geometry — preserve it. Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room.

prep.what: Add wall height as a project-level setting, preserve room perimeter through the seeder, and emit wall paint SF (perimeter × height) as a seeded estimate line item.
prep.understand: The takeoff gives floor area and room perimeter from 2D geometry. Wall height is the third dimension you have to add. `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` currently calls the engine, maps measurement data to line items, and silently drops `geometry.rings` and `meta.perimeter`. Without perimeter, you can't compute wall area. The fix has two parts: (1) stop dropping perimeter, (2) add a `wall_height_ft` field to estimates so the seeder has a height to multiply by. This is what makes CT Pros' core trade — painting — actually estimable from a blueprint.
approach: Write a migration adding `wall_height_ft` nullable decimal (default 8.0) to the `estimates` table. Apply locally and verify no existing tests break.
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop dropping `meta.perimeter` from the engine's room data — store it in a local variable alongside `area` and `room_name`.

Compute `wall_paint_sf = meta_perimeter * estimate->wall_height_ft` per room. Emit a new line item: `kind='area'`, `surface='wall_paint'`, `unit='sqft'`, `quantity=wall_paint_sf`, `description='Wall paint — {room_name}'`.
Add a `wall_height_ft` number input to the Takeoff Vue UI or estimate form (default 8). Wire it to the estimate model so the seeder picks it up on next seed.
Write a seeder test: given a mock room with `meta.perimeter=40` and `wall_height_ft=8`, assert the output line item has `quantity=320` and `surface='wall_paint'`.
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — file to modify; find where it processes room data from the engine response

prep.what: Replace the single-anonymous-line seeder with a type switch that routes each measurement kind to the correct trade (flooring, painting, trim, doors) using the existing core-vs-subbed helpers.
prep.understand: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` ignores measurement kind and collapses everything into `kind=custom`, $0, dropping trade context. The engine API returns measurements with a `kind` field: `area` (floor SF), `line` (LF — walls/trim), `count` (each — doors/fixtures). After t45 you also have a derived `wall_paint` surface. The `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` helper (from t36) already knows which trades CT Pros self-performs vs subcontracts — use it to decide `fromLaborRate()` vs `fromSubcontract()` per line.
approach: Read the engine API measurement response shape (check `sdk/laravel/TakeoffClient.php` or the `/measurements` route) — understand what `kind` values come back and what each carries.
Write a `$tradeForKind` map or helper in `TakeoffEstimateSeeder`: `'area'→'flooring'`, `'wall_paint'→'painting'`, `'line'→'trim'`, `'count'→'door'`.

In the seeder loop, switch on kind and call the right `LineItemFactory` method: core trades (painting, flooring) → `fromLaborRate()` with matching LaborRate; sub trades (trim, tile) → `fromSubcontract()`. Pull the right rate by trade name from the DB.
Verify against `LaborRateSeeder.php` — make sure painting and flooring rates exist by name (from t39). If trim is missing, note it for t47 (PerLinearFt RateType).
Write seeder tests: area measurement → flooring line item; line measurement → trim line item (subcontract); count → door line item.
